ledger.claim: If the case is to turn on whether this rider should bear the fee at all, that question is not settled by the record and the answer the policy gives is escalation rather than collection. Rider presence is the only fact that speaks to the rider's side of the no-show test, and the only artifact that touches it is the trace, whose rider leg is filtered out in its entirety; POL-NS-04(c) says in terms that this leaves the artifact impaired for the purposes of POL-NS-08(b), and where the sole evidence for a fact is impaired under limb (b) the matter escalates under POL-NS-09 instead of being resolved against the party it disfavours. I again disclose that the chat artifact I cite to show the rider was never reached is impaired (UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85, per POL-GEN-02(1)). Escalation is terminal and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles the open question: whether a rider who was inside Terminal 3, whose arrival notice was never read and whom the driver never telephoned, should be charged a no-show fee on a trace that cannot place him at all.

I do not press the two arithmetic routes that are closed to the rider, and I do not ask the judge to stretch them. The derived dwell is a single continuous qualifying run of 620 seconds — 63 fixes from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05 inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius — against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum, a surplus of 140 seconds (shortfall_sec -140.0), so no waiting-period shortfall argument under POL-NS-06 is available; and the same derived facts put the driver in-radius and holding position 25 seconds before he tapped 'arrived' at 23:13:10, so no false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 is available either. The rider's case rests on the points above, not on those.

Limb (a) of the chargeable-no-show test is met on the face of the record: the trip record for TRP-00202 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-24T23:13:10+08:00, and the trip is recorded as cancelled by the driver, not abandoned before arrival.

Limb (b) is met: the driver's GPS trace has him inside the AIRPORT arrival radius of 150 m at and before the arrival event — the qualifying in-geofence run opens at 23:12:45, a full 25 seconds before the 23:13:10 arrival marker, and the trace's closest approach to the pin is 22.4 m, far inside the 150 m radius the fee schedule sets for the Changi kerbside.

Limb (c) is met with room to spare: the driver held position inside the geofence in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 GPS fixes lasting 620 seconds, from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05. That clears the 480-second AIRPORT minimum by 140 seconds; the shortfall field reads -140.0, i.e. a surplus, and limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap, which is exactly how this run is computed.

Limb (d) is met: the trip record shows no boarding event and records the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW at 23:23:20 — fifteen seconds AFTER the required 480-second dwell elapsed at 23:23:05, so the cancellation falls at or after the moment the dwell was complete as limb (d) requires. The reason code is one of the three limb (d) recognises, and this is not a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE case that would divert the matter to POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not defeat the fee, because the arrival marker is not false. At 23:13:10 the driver was already stationary inside the 150 m radius — the dwell had opened 25 seconds earlier — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at or above the 15 km/h motion threshold at the moment the marker was set. The clause's own limb (iii) confirms a marker set by a driver who then genuinely waits the full period does not void an otherwise good fee.

Limb (a) requires a rider chat message that locates or coordinates, and the chat log contains only the system 'driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages — there is no rider message at all, so limb (a) fails before limb (b) or (c) is reached. Limb (c) would in any event be undecidable rather than satisfied: every one of the rider's 88 fixes reports 45 m to 80 m horizontal accuracy and is filtered out, leaving rider_qualifying_fix_count at 0, which POL-NS-04 expressly makes neutral rather than adverse.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

To the rider: I accept that your flight was delayed and that you say you were inside Terminal 3 the whole time. The $6 charge, however, is a driver no-show fee, and the rule that makes it chargeable (POL-NS-01) turns on what the driver did, not on where you were. On this record all four conditions are met. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 23:13:10. (b) The GPS trace places the driver inside the 150 m Terminal 3 arrival radius at and before that event: his qualifying run opens at 23:12:45, 25 seconds earlier, and his closest approach to the pin is 22.4 m. (c) He held position in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 fixes lasting 620 seconds, from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05 — 140 seconds more than the 480 seconds an AIRPORT pickup requires, measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the tap. (d) The trip record shows no boarding and a driver termination at 23:23:20 with the recognised reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, i.e. fifteen seconds after the required wait had elapsed. The fee therefore stands as charged.

I have considered the points your representative raised. The rider leg of the trace cannot place you, because every one of its 88 fixes reports 45–80 m accuracy and so falls outside the 25 m filter; that leg is undecidable and neutral rather than evidence you were elsewhere, and I say so. But that neutrality does not decide this case, because the no-show fee does not depend on your position, and the one clause that turns on rider position and messages (POL-NS-04) requires that you yourself sent a locating or coordinating message during the wait. The chat log contains none — only the system arrival notice and two driver messages — so limb (a) of POL-NS-04 fails and that clause does not apply. Your further point that the case should escalate because rider presence is unproved is rejected: rider presence is not a deciding fact for a fee that turns on the driver, so it is not 'the sole evidence for the deciding fact', and no escalation trigger fires. The escalation limb the policy gives for an impaired sole carrier (POL-NS-09(e)) is therefore not reached, and neither is the contradiction limb (POL-NS-09(b)): the trip record's 10.2-minute wait and the trace's 620-second dwell agree.

Disclosure and weight. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00202) is impaired at weight 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE, and the driver profile (EV-DPROF-00202) is impaired at weight 0.9, issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH; I have named both, as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. Neither carries the deciding facts. The arrival, the dwell and the termination are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record, both at full weight 1.0, and the fee by the fare breakdown at 1.0; the driver-profile counters are consulted only for the anti-farming check and the finding survives the 0.9 discount because 1 termination across 168 trips sits an order of magnitude below both thresholds. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00202-01, weight 0.0) carries nothing and is immaterial: the plain dwell already exceeds the minimum, so the limb (i) accumulation route is not needed and its absence is not held against anyone. Confidence is set at 0.9, the weight of the lowest artifact the compensation outcome relies on, which is above the 0.70 floor. No route to refund is open: there is no shortfall under POL-NS-06 (620 > 480), and no false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05 because the driver was stationary inside the zone when he tapped.

To the driver: your account is corroborated by the trace rather than merely asserted. Under POL-NS-07 you are entitled to 80 percent of the $6.00 fee, SGD 4.80, charged to the platform, with the residual 20 percent retained as the service fee. The anti-farming check does not bite: 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below 4, and 1/168 is far below the 0.08 rate test. Because the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount_sgd carries the same SGD 4.80 figure as driver_compensation_sgd; this is the sum the ruling moves and is not a further payment. The rider's charge stands. No referral is produced, because no false-arrival record arises and no billing-integrity or conduct review is engaged.
